title: This Fried Pork Got 100M Views and Its Own Office in China | China Travel Expert
description:
Guobaorou (锅包肉) — crispy sweet-and-sour fried pork — went so viral in China that in 2024 the city of Jilin held a "World Guobaorou Competition" and floated setting up an official Guobaorou Office. The topic passed 100 million views on Douyin.

The dish was created in Harbin around 1907 by chef Zheng Xingwen, who turned a savoury fried-pork strip into a sweet-and-sour version for foreign guests. Today the north argues over it: Heilongjiang and Jilin keep the amber sugar-and-vinegar glaze, while Liaoning coats it in tomato ketchup — same dish, two camps.

🧭 Expert Tip: In Northeast China (Dongbei), ask for "laoshi" (老式) if you want the classic amber vinegar-sugar version rather than the red ketchup one.
